title: Module 4 assessment
subtitle: Logical, Text and Date Functions
description: Fifteen questions across the whole of Module 4. Every question explains its answer, right or wrong.

questions.question: B2 holds a score. Write a formula returning "Pass" when it is 40 or more and "Fail" otherwise.
questions.explanation: Condition, then value if true, then value if false. The commonest error is omitting the last argument - IF(B2>=40,"Pass") returns FALSE rather than "Fail", which looks like a bug but is Excel doing exactly what you asked.

questions.question: You are writing a seventh nested IF. What does that suggest?
options: A lookup table with VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP is the right structure
questions.explanation: Beyond three or four levels, the logic is really a table of bands - and a table can be read, changed and audited by someone who does not write formulas. IFS flattens the syntax but keeps the rules locked inside the formula.

questions.question: `=AND(A1>10,B1<5)` returns TRUE when either condition is met.
questions.explanation: AND needs every condition true; OR needs at least one. The mix-up is easy to make and produces plausible-looking results, which is why it is worth testing a logical formula against a row you know should fail.

questions.question: What is the practical difference between IFERROR and IFNA?
options: IFERROR catches every error; IFNA catches only #N/A
questions.explanation: That difference matters on a lookup. IFERROR hides a genuine #REF! or #VALUE! alongside the expected 'not found', so a broken formula returns your tidy message instead of alerting you. On lookups, prefer IFNA.

questions.question: An imported name column will not match your master list, though the names look identical. What do you check first?
options: Trailing spaces, with TRIM and LEN
questions.explanation: LEN on both versions shows the difference immediately - 'Anil Kumar ' is eleven characters against ten. TRIM strips leading, trailing and repeated internal spaces. It is the most common cause of a lookup that should work and does not.

questions.question: `=LEN("  Anil  Kumar  ")` returns 15. What does `=LEN(TRIM("  Anil  Kumar  "))` return?
questions.explanation: TRIM removes the leading and trailing spaces and collapses the double space between the words to one, leaving 'Anil Kumar' at ten characters. It does not remove every space - only the ones that are not single separators.

questions.question: SUBSTITUTE is case-sensitive.
questions.explanation: SUBSTITUTE("Ltd","ltd","Limited") finds nothing, because the case differs. REPLACE, by contrast, works by position and ignores content entirely - use SUBSTITUTE when you know the text, REPLACE when you know where it sits.

questions.question: Which function joins a list of names with commas and skips the blank cells?
options: TEXTJOIN with its second argument TRUE
questions.explanation: TEXTJOIN(", ",TRUE,A2:A20) handles the delimiter and the gaps in one go. CONCAT joins everything including blanks, leaving ', ,' where the gaps were - cleaning that up afterwards is the slow path.

questions.question: DOB is in B2. Write a formula giving completed age in whole years as at today.
questions.explanation: DATEDIF is undocumented - it does not appear in Excel's function list - but it is the correct tool for completed years and handles leap years properly. Subtracting dates and dividing by 365 drifts by a day every four years.

questions.question: `=NETWORKDAYS("01-Oct-2024","07-Oct-2024")` returns what, with no holidays given?
questions.explanation: It counts both endpoints and excludes Saturdays and Sundays. 1 to 7 October 2024 spans a weekend, leaving five working days. Pass a holiday range as the third argument to exclude public holidays too.

questions.question: Grading into five bands by score. Nested IFs or a lookup table with approximate match?
options: IFS - it is cleaner than nesting
A lookup table - the bands become data the business owner can change
questions.explanation: Both work, but only one lets the policy change without editing a formula. Put the bands in a labelled table and anyone can adjust a threshold; bury them in a formula and every change needs you.

questions.question: A blank cell is ignored by a comparison like `=IF(B2>100,...)`, so that row is skipped.
questions.explanation: It is not skipped - blank evaluates as 0, which is fine for a greater-than test and dangerous for a less-than one - an empty cell passes `<100` and quietly joins your result set. Test for the blank explicitly when it could mean 'not yet known'.

questions.question: A report shows #N/A in thirty rows and the manager wants it to look clean. What is the right response?
options: Wrap every lookup in IFERROR and move on
Find out why thirty rows do not match, then handle the genuine misses with IFNA
questions.explanation: #N/A is information - thirty unmatched records usually means a data problem worth knowing about. Hide it first and you ship a clean-looking report built on thirty gaps.

questions.question: `=NOT(A1="Active")` is equivalent to which of these?
questions.explanation: NOT inverts a logical result, and <> is the not-equal operator, so both return TRUE when the status is anything but Active. The operator form is usually easier to read inside a longer condition.

questions.question: Why wrap a date in TEXT() when joining it into a sentence?
options: Because joining a date with & gives the serial number, not the date
questions.explanation: `="Due "&B2` returns 'Due 45200'. `="Due "&TEXT(B2,"dd-mmm-yyyy")` returns 'Due 07-Oct-2024'. The & operator converts to raw text, and a date's raw text is its serial number.
